title: Quasi-coherence of the tensor pushout algebra
statement: Let $f:U\to X$ be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Put $A=f_*\mathcal O_U$, let $r_0:f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_U$ be the structure map and $t_0:f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to f^{-1}A$ the inverse image of $\mathcal O_X\to A$. For any pushout square of commutative ring sheaves with legs $b:\mathcal O_U\to B$ and $t:f^{-1}A\to B$, the underlying $\mathcal O_U$-module of the algebra $(B,b)$ is quasi-coherent [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf, pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01SB (lemma-affine-equivalence-modules), construction of h and elucidation

proof.text: The underlying module of A is quasi-coherent by the affine direct-image algebra theorem. Pulling it back to U preserves quasi-coherence.

On sections the tensor algebra is the pushout of the two commutative algebras, and sheafification extends this universal property to ring sheaves. The two universal properties provide inverse O_U-algebra maps between the given B and the sheafified tensor algebra. Its underlying module is the tensor-formula pullback of the module A. Transfer quasi-coherence along this module isomorphism.

proof_origin.note: Details of the tensor construction and elucidation of Stacks 01SB, read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01SB.
